the N-subdomain of HipA, far from the active site, is critical for HipA function, that HipA–HipBA promoter complexes form higher-order complexes in which HipA forms dimmers via the N-subdomain, and that the N-subdomains of HipA are critical for HipA dimerization.
HipA–HipBA complexes form higher-order structures that occlude HipA’s active site.

the molecular mechanisms that govern the emergence and persistence of antibiotic resistance.
the mechanisms of bacterial persistence, the ability of bacteria to survive in the presence of otherwise lethal concentrations of antibiotics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HipA kinase is a critical determinant of persister cell formation and that mutations within HipA N-subdomain-2, which is distant from the active site, result in increased persister cell formation.

(1) HipBA–promoter complexes provide a mechanism for the regulation of multidrug tolerance in E. coli. (2) High-persister hipB and hipA mutants cause heritable multidrug resistance in E. coli and are responsible for chronic urinary tract infections.

we have identified the genetic and molecular basis of heritable drug tolerance, which is the main cause of antibiotic resistance.

the HipA–HipBA promoter structure is the basis of heritability of antibiotic tolerance.

the HipBA locus encodes an antibiotic tolerance factor.
